description: Shared cross-language case table for the canary arm-assignment rule (canary agent releases). Consumed verbatim by backend/src/lambda/utils/__tests__/canary-assignment.parity.test.ts and arbiter/governance/__tests__/test_canary_assignment_parity.py. Do not hand-copy into either suite — both load this file directly. Region hashes use the SAME normalization as grandfathering-parity-cases.json (drop comment/blank lines, strip trailing backslash, canonicalize quotes to ', collapse whitespace, join kept lines with a single space, sha256 of the UTF-8 result).

regionHashes.hashAlgorithm: sha256 of the NORMALIZED substring strictly between 'PARITY-GUARD:BEGIN' (exclusive) and 'PARITY-GUARD:END' (exclusive). Normalization identical to grandfathering-parity-cases.json.

cases.description: percentBasisPoints=0 routes every key to stable regardless of hash
percentBasisPoints=10000 routes every key to candidate (promote-to-100 shape)
an empty stickiness key degrades to the safe stable arm, never candidate
user-x hashes to bucket 1200 under salt-A; at 15% it is below threshold -> candidate
user-x hashes to bucket 1200 under salt-A; at 10% it is at/above threshold -> stable
orch-42 hashes to bucket 1817 under salt-A; threshold exactly 1817 -> stable (bucket < threshold is strict; this is the MUST-BITE case for a < vs <= mutant)
conv-3 bucket 6104 under salt-A; at 70% -> candidate
conv-3 bucket 6104 under salt-A; at 50% -> stable
a negative percent clamps to 0 -> stable, never throws
conv-3 bucket 6104; 6105.9 floors to 6105 so 6104 < 6105 -> candidate (floor applied before compare)
orch-42 bucket 1817 under salt-A; at 50% -> candidate
orch-42 hashes to bucket 8135 under salt-B; at 50% -> stable. Same key+percent, different salt, different arm: proves a fresh episode salt re-buckets deliberately
